quote: Is this kind of your first time, looking into solar, or have you looked into it before?
stewart_read: The rep asks whether this is the customer's first look at solar but never asks WHY they're interested in solar at all — the emotional anchor question from the script is skipped entirely in favor of a first-time/repeat framing.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the move-in timing as self-evident motivation (new homeowner prepping the house) and treated that as sufficient context.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always ask the direct 'what interested you in solar' question — even a one-line answer gives the closer something to anchor on, and here nothing was captured.

quote: all we ask of the homeowner is you just have a credit score of at least 670. Is that gonna be an issue for you at all?
stewart_read: Rep states the correct 670 threshold (no drift here) and asks directly, which is clean qualifier execution.
coaching_implication: No coaching needed here — this is the correct script number and phrasing; useful as a contrast if other reps drift on this number.

quote: Cool. Well, we the last thing we'll need is just the square footage of the home. Do you happen to know that off the top of your head? If not, I can look it up.
stewart_read: Rep moves straight from the cash-deal answer to square footage without ever asking about the utility bill amount — the qualifying checklist item that most directly creates urgency is bypassed entirely.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be relying on the specialist call to gather bill info from the customer directly, treating this as an organic-lead pattern where bill isn't required pre-appointment.
coaching_implication: Flag that the bill amount question was never asked at all — not deferred, not declined, simply never raised. This is the single biggest missed anchor on the call.

quote: Well, we are good to go in getting this design built out for you. The last thing I need to know now is just a good time for my specialist to give you a call to go over that design as well as answer any questions or concerns you may have.
stewart_read: Rep holds scope cleanly here — no attempt to explain design mechanics, pricing, or equipment; the handoff to the specialist is immediate and appropriate.
coaching_implication: Positive example to reinforce — this is the correct universal escape hatch pattern and should be named as a strength in the 1-on-1, not just gaps.

quote: 9AM. K. All this is the call. Correct? And this is all all this is the call. Correct? Yes, sir. This is just a phone call.
stewart_read: Rep confirms the appointment time and channel but never runs the explicit 'is that fair?' handshake or a clear one-hour block statement — the button-up is compressed and missing its verbal-commitment mechanics.
alternative_hypothesis: The call's overall brevity and cooperative tone may have made the rep judge the handshake as unnecessary friction for an already-agreeable customer.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always land the explicit fairness check and hour-block statement, even on easy, cooperative calls — it's the mechanic tied to show-rate, not just formality.

quote: K. I appreciate your time, sir. We'll look forward to speaking with you tomorrow at nine.
stewart_read: Call ends without the rep stating he'll send a confirmation text — the passive 'look forward to speaking with you' close substitutes for the required text-followup promise.
coaching_implication: Small but consistent gap — pair with the 02:something handshake miss as one button-up coaching thread for this rep.
